articles.title: Middleton's Regeneration Accelerates with Key Developments Announced
articles.excerpt: Middleton's regeneration initiative has gained momentum with three significant announcements, including plans for the historic Middleton Old Grammar School and the repurposing of the Scout Hut for community use.
articles.content_html:
Middleton's regeneration initiative has taken a significant step forward with three key announcements made during an event at Middleton Arena on 16 September 2026. The event, attended by over 500 residents and local business leaders, was chaired by the proposed chairs of Middleton's Mayoral Development Corporation, Steve Coogan and Rose Marley, alongside Greater Manchester Mayor Bev Craig and Rochdale Borough Council leader, Councillor Neil Emmott.

One of the major announcements involved the historic Middleton Old Grammar School, located on Boarshaw Road. Recently acquired by the council, the school, which dates back to 1582, is expected to announce a new tenant by the end of the year. The council plans to conduct a feasibility study to assess the building's repair and refurbishment, aiming to reopen it for community use in the future. Previously, the site served as a wedding and events venue before being purchased by the council when it became available for sale.

In addition to the school, the council is also in the process of acquiring the long-derelict Warwick Mill and the adjacent London House office block. The aim is to restore Warwick Mill for residential use while demolishing London House. This move is part of a broader strategy to revitalise the area and enhance local housing options.

Furthermore, the Middleton Scout Hut on Long Street, which has been vacant for 13 years, will be transformed into a community venue. The council has secured a long-term lease with the Groundwork Trust, a charitable organisation, to repurpose the building. Plans include creating a hub for workshops focused on ecology and construction skills, as well as providing a space for local environmental projects and activities aimed at young people, thereby addressing social isolation within the community.
